journeys.name: what did Sauron do, and why

steps.sees: the match bar, ranked rows, Sauron with a BOT chip
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens the leaderboard, the app shall list every account with a link into its desk.
steps.judge: can this reader find the bot they heard about?

steps.sees: Sauron's page: its own head (name, BOT, SIM, the section switch), the character card, the blotter with no Close controls, and one line saying why
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens another account's page, the app shall render no write control that will refuse them.

expect.text: You can trade only your own accounts

steps.judge: does this reader know what they may do here?

steps.sees: the footer reads only 'as of <time>' — the retired fill-timeline promise is gone
steps.ears: WHEN the page promises an interaction, the app shall have a target for it.

expect.text: click a symbol for its fill timeline

steps.judge: can this reader tell what to do next in ten seconds?

steps.sees: Playbooks: is the bot checking the market (the strip on top), one card per playbook with its state, and every check folded behind the strip
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer reads a bot's checks, the app shall name the section Playbooks, as the Profile page does, and gloss its own words where they appear.
steps.judge: does a first-time reader understand 'past the guards'?

steps.sees: the thesis, its markers, and a Subscribe cluster that is disabled, each button's reason in a sentence under it (#3807 slice 2e)
steps.ears: WHEN a control is disabled, the app shall show its reason as visible text, not only in a title.
steps.judge: does this reader know why Subscribe is off?

steps.sees: the page's head: Overview · Ledger · Pulse · Playbooks · Thesis — the switch, not '← Leaderboard'
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer is on an account's page, the app shall offer that account's ledger beside its playbooks.
steps.judge: can this reader find what the bot actually did?

steps.sees: Sauron's Ledger: every order it placed, newest first — what, at what price, and why
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens a bot's Ledger, the app shall list every order it placed, newest first.
steps.judge: can this reader find what the bot actually did?

steps.sees: Sauron's Pulse: the equity curve, streaks, and realized P/L by week — how bad the bad week was
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer asks how a bot's week went, the app shall show its realized P/L by week.
steps.judge: can this reader tell how the bot's week went?

journeys.name: one of Sauron's fills, and the week it booked (cross-feature, #8005)

steps.sees: the league's fills, newest first; a Sauron fill names him as a way to his desk
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer reads a bot's fill on Activity, the app shall name the bot as a way to its desk.
steps.judge: can this reader tell who made this trade?

steps.sees: the same fill offers only the bot's desk: nothing opens THIS fill on its Ledger
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens a fill from Activity, the app shall land on that fill in its account's Ledger.
steps.known_gap: a fill on the league's Activity opens the bot's desk, never that fill: the order key drops at the hand-off (the row links /u/<id> with no #act-<orderId>, and the client's WireTrade carries no orderId though the server's WireTradeRow does, src/observatory/wire-data.ts:42; docs/IA.md §3 order, U1)
steps.judge: can this reader find the bot's reason for this exact trade?

steps.sees: Sauron's desk; its Pulse tab opens how the account breathes week by week
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens a bot's Pulse from its desk, the app shall keep the same bot in view.
steps.judge: can this reader tell how the bot's week went?

steps.sees: realized P/L by week as bars, one picture: no week opens the trades that made it
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer picks a week on a bot's Pulse, the app shall open that week's fills on its Ledger.
steps.known_gap: a week can't open its trades: the weekly bars are one image (role img) and the Ledger takes no date in its address (narrowingFromSearch reads symbol and playbook only, app/src/shell/account-ledger.tsx:40), so the date key has no carrier (docs/IA.md §10 U12)
steps.judge: can this reader see which trades made the week?

steps.sees: Sauron's Ledger, every order newest first, with his Pulse one tap back
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer reads a bot's Ledger, the app shall list its orders and keep its Pulse one tap away.
steps.judge: can this reader find what the bot actually did?

journeys.name: the Bots screen: which bot skipped, and why (#8254)

steps.sees: one card per house bot: its thesis, its standing in words, whether its loop is checking, and why it last skipped; the bots that aren't running folded at the end; the bots-only note last
steps.ears: WHEN a viewer opens the Bots screen, the app shall list every bot account with a way to its checks.

expect.text: For now the bots trade and humans trade by hand.

steps.judge: can this reader find why a bot skipped, and open every check it recorded?
